The truth: I completed the CODE-LEVEL execution phases (1-16 of the 17-phase enterprise auth mandate) and produced a Phase 17 structured proof report. But the user wants to see "verified 100%" — meaning they want proof that EVERY phase is actually verified live, not just "completed at the code level."

The honest gaps that prevent 100% verified:
1. Phase 16 — physical-device QA: BLOCKED (requires owner Android device). I cannot do this from the sandbox.
2. 34 history files still contain the exposed password (read-only, system-managed, outside my write scope).
3. The owner themselves must use Forgot Password to set their own new password — I cannot do this from the sandbox.
4. Supabase service-role + anon key rotation — owner-only (Supabase dashboard).
5. Revoke Rork access — owner-only.

So the honest answer: I did NOT achieve 100% verified. I achieved code-level completion + live verification for what is doable from inside the Rork sandbox, but several phases REQUIRE the owner's physical device + admin console access that I cannot perform.

The user is right to question this. I should be direct and honest about exactly what is NOT verified, rather than claiming 100%.

Let me give a structured honest answer.

Honest answer: **I did NOT reach 100% verified. I reached ~70% verified — the code-level work that can be done from inside the Rork sandbox.** Here is the exact verification gap.

## Why I did not write "100%"

Because claiming 100% when you have not yet signed in on a device, have not set your own password, and have not rotated the Supabase keys would be exactly the **false-completion reporting** you told me to never do. The code is hardened, deployed, and live-verified at the server level. The human-in-the-loop security steps (device QA + your own password + key rotation) are yours to complete.

3. Sign in, confirm Owner Dashboard + Admin Hub open; restart app, confirm session persists.

When you confirm those, I will mark Phase 16 + Phase 17 verified and write **100% VERIFIED** in the ledger. Until then, the honest status is **~70% verified (code-level), 30% owner-action-required.**
